observations: Three photos show a used car engine on a stand in a workshop or garage.
The engine has visible wear, rust, and grime, especially on the timing cover and belts.
The engine is mounted on a metal stand with a pulley system visible at the bottom.
The engine block has a label with a barcode and some text, but it is too blurry to read.
The engine appears to be a V6 or V8, based on the number of cylinders and components.
There are stickers on the engine cover, including orange and purple ones, possibly for identification or protection.
The watermark 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' is overlaid on all photos, suggesting the seller's branding.
No visible damage to the block or major components, but internal condition is unknown.

claims.claim: We all so deals on in all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: The seller's text is a general statement about their business, not specific to this item. No proof of stock or variety is visible in the photos.

claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: Engine may be damaged internally (e.g., blown head gasket, cracked block, worn bearings)
risks.proof: A video showing the engine running or a compression test report.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working or severely damaged

risks.risk: Engine may have been in a wrecked or accident-damaged vehicle
risks.proof: Photos of the vehicle it came from, or a vehicle history report.
risks.if_unproven: priced as salvage or unknown provenance

risks.risk: Engine may not be compatible with the buyer's vehicle (e.g., wrong VIN or model)
risks.proof: Clear photo of the engine block with visible casting number or VIN tag.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the engine block showing casting number or VIN tag.
Video of the engine running or a compression test report.
Photos of the vehicle it came from, if available.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
